steps.say: Prune belly syndrome is diagnosed across the room by its wrinkled abdomen, but the triad behind the wrinkles decides the workup. The baby shows deficient abdominal wall muscles with loose prune-like skin, both testes stuck inside the belly, and a massively dilated urinary tract. This Eagle Barrett triad is almost exclusive to boys and signals a long reconstructive road.
steps.tx: Diagnose **Prune belly syndrome** (**Eagle-Barrett**, wrinkled belly disease) by the **classic triad** (three linked defects): deficient abdominal musculature (lax prune skin), bilateral **cryptorchidism** (undescended testes), and dilated tortuous urinary tract (**megacystis-megaureter**, giant bladder and ureters). The triad clusters in boys and forecasts renal dysplasia, so stage kidneys, testes, and wall together at diagnosis.

vis.caption: Paediatric urological conditions: prune belly triad spans wall, testes, and tract. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A prune belly urethra looks like valves on scans but scopes clean, and that distinction changes everything. Prostatic hypoplasia leaves the back urethra wide and floppy instead of valved, so urine stagnates from poor pumping rather than blockage. Stasis without obstruction means no ablation helps: management drains and watches rather than cuts.
steps.tx: Separate prune belly from valves by scoping: **prostatic hypoplasia** (undergrown prostate) with **dilated posterior urethra** (wide floppy back channel) causes functional stasis without mechanical valves. No leaflets mean no ablation target, so treatment is drainage, timed voiding, and infection control while the floppy system grows. Misreading stasis as obstruction invites a useless destructive scope.

steps.say: Reconstruction is completed on the whole front in one infancy operation, not piecemeal over years. The Monfort abdominoplasty pleats the lax wall muscles into a firm corset, bilateral transabdominal orchiopexy drags both testes into the scrotum through the same opening, and selected megaureters are tapered and reimplanted. One coordinated sitting under one anaesthetic resets wall, testes, and drainage together.
steps.tx: Reconstruct comprehensively in infancy: **Monfort plication** (**abdominoplasty**, wall tightening pleats) firms the abdominal corset, **bilateral orchiopexy** (both testes brought down transabdominally) places gonads for surveillance and fertility, and selective ureteral tapering with reimplantation narrows mantis limbs. Combined wall, gonad, and tract surgery under one anaesthetic beats staged piecemeal repair for growth and family burden.

vis.alt: Illustration of undescended testis examination with milking technique.
vis.caption: Undescended testes in prune belly: bilateral orchiopexy places both for surveillance. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The urachus is the leftover pipe from bladder to belly button, and when it refuses to close it leaks urine at the navel. A patent urachus, half of all urachal anomalies, means the whole allantoic duct stayed open, so the baby dribbles clear urine continuously from the umbilicus. Any wet navel beyond the cord stump falling off earns a probe and a scan.
steps.tx: Suspect **patent urachus** (open navel pipe, **50%**, fifty in a hundred, of urachal anomalies) when clear fluid wets the umbilicus: complete failure of the **allantoic duct** (fetal bladder stalk) to obliterate leaves **umbilical urinary drainage** (urine leaking at the navel). Confirm with sinogram or ultrasound tracing the tract to the bladder dome, then excise the whole channel since infected remnants recur.

steps.say: When only the middle of the pipe stays open, the trapped pocket grows into a time bomb below the navel. A urachal cyst forms where both ends seal but the centre stays patent, and it announces itself as an infected midline lump under the belly button with fever and tenderness. Incision alone fails, because the leftover lining reforms, so complete excision follows infection control.
steps.tx: Drain then excise the midline lump: **urachal cyst** (**30%**, thirty in a hundred) arises with both ends closed and the centre patent, presenting as an infected **infraumbilical mass** (below navel swelling) that is tender and febrile. Antibiotics cool the abscess first, then total cyst excision removes the secretory lining, because drainage alone leaves epithelium that refills and reinfects.

steps.say: A navel that oozes pus on and off hides a blind tunnel pointing at the bladder. The urachal sinus opens at the umbilicus and dives toward the dome without connecting, discharging intermittent purulent or blood tinged fluid that antibiotics pause but never end. Probing maps the dead end, and excision of the whole tract cures the discharge for good.
steps.tx: Trace the discharging navel: **urachal sinus** (blind navel tunnel) runs from umbilicus toward the dome without bladder entry, leaking intermittent **purulent discharge** (pus or serosanguinous ooze) that flares between antibiotic courses. Sinogram outlines the dead end for complete excision, because partial shaving leaves epithelium that suppurates again within months.

steps.say: The urachus can turn malignant decades later, and its cancer breaks bladder rules. Urachal carcinoma is an aggressive adenocarcinoma growing from intestinal metaplasia at the bladder dome, causing under half a percent of all bladder cancers. Blood in the urine or mucus threads in an adult with a midline dome mass is treated as urachus until proven otherwise, because ordinary urothelial tumours spare the dome.
steps.tx: Respect the dome mass: **urachal carcinoma** (navel pipe cancer) is an aggressive **adenocarcinoma** (gland forming cancer) from intestinal metaplasia at the **bladder dome** (bladder roof), under **0.5%** (under half in a hundred) of bladder cancers. Mucus in urine with a midline dome lesion clinches suspicion, and staging must exclude colorectal and ovarian mimics that also seed the midline.

steps.say: Urachal cancer surgery removes the whole embryonic field, not just the lump. En bloc partial cystectomy takes the bladder dome with the entire urachus, the median umbilical ligament, and the belly button in one unbroken specimen. Breaking the chain or sparing the navel for cosmesis seeds recurrence along the leftover tract, so the umbilicus is always sacrificed.
steps.tx: Resect the whole field with **en bloc excision** (unbroken removal): **partial cystectomy** (dome bladder removal) with complete urachus, median umbilical ligament, and **umbilectomy** (navel removal) in one specimen. The chain from dome to skin goes together because skip lesions hide along the tract, and piecemeal surgery converts a curable dome cancer into an incurable abdominal wall recurrence.
